comment: Phone-number rules keyed by country. Shipped, read-only, editable without a rebuild — the same rule as the tax presets beside this file. 'dialCode' is the international calling code shown in front of the number and stored with it ('+1 905-401-6667'). 'nationalDigits' lists the digit counts a NATIONAL number may have in that country, excluding the dial code: Canada and the US are exactly 10 (NANP), China's mobiles are 11, Japan is 10 or 11, France and Spain are 9. A number is checked against the country PICKED FOR IT, never against the shop's own — a Toronto shop takes a visiting customer's Shanghai mobile, and validating that against Canada would refuse a correct number.
separateFromTaxComment: This is a SEPARATE file from tax-jurisdictions.json even though the codes overlap today, because they answer different questions and are not the same list. A shop's location is one of the markets this build sells INTO; a phone country is anywhere a customer's number can come FROM. Merging them would mean either shipping tax presets for countries the app does not trade in, or refusing numbers from countries it does not.
formatComment: 'nationalFormat' groups a number as it is typed. Keyed by DIGIT COUNT, because a country can write two lengths differently: '#' takes the next digit and anything else is punctuation, emitted only when a digit still follows it, so a half-typed number never shows a trailing dash. A digit count with no entry is NOT formatted — the number is left exactly as typed. Japan's 10-digit numbers are deliberately absent: 03-1234-5678 and 045-123-4567 are both correct and nothing in the digits themselves says which grouping applies, so guessing would mis-punctuate half the country. Its 11-digit mobiles are unambiguous and are grouped.
patternComment: 'nationalPattern' is matched against the DIGITS of a national number, with all punctuation already stripped, and is what actually decides whether a number is possible in that country. It catches what counting digits cannot: a Canadian area code starting with 0 or 1, a Chinese mobile not starting with 1, a Japanese number missing its trunk 0 — each of these has exactly the right number of digits and is still not a number that country issues. A country shipping no pattern falls back to 'nationalDigits' alone, so adding one is optional and removing one is safe. A pattern that does not compile is ignored with the same fallback rather than taking the country down.
patternSourceComment: CA/US: NANP — area code and exchange are both N-X-X, so neither may begin 0 or 1. CN: 11-digit mobiles are 1 followed by 3-9. FR: the national significant number drops the trunk 0, so it never starts with one. ES: mobiles begin 6 or 7, landlines 8 or 9.
japanHasNoPatternComment: Japan ships no 'nationalPattern' ON PURPOSE, for the same reason it ships no 10-digit 'nationalFormat': both conventions are in use here and the digits do not say which. '090-1234-5678' carries the domestic trunk 0 at 11 digits, while '90-1234-5678' is the same mobile written internationally at 10, and '03-1234-5678' is a Tokyo landline at 10 WITH the zero. A pattern demanding a leading zero refuses the second; one forbidding it refuses the third. Length alone is the only rule that is true of all three, so length alone is the rule.
